exampleAnswers.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2}.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 3 \\ 2x_1 + x_2 = 8 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 8 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + (-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 3 \\ x_2 = 2. \end{cases} \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3 \mathbf{a_1} + 2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 3 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 3 \cdot 2 = 6.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-x_2 = 1 \\ x_2 = 1 \\ 2x_1+3x_2 = 7 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 7 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3-5R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-x_2 = 1 \\ x_2 = 1 \\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2=1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1- 1 = 1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=2. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2\mathbf{a_1} + \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 2 \cdot 1 = 2.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 2 \\ 2x_1+4x_2 = 0 \\ -3x_1+x_2 =-7 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & -7 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 2 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & -7 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3+3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{1}{4} R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 2 \\ x_2 = -1 \\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2 \mathbf{a_1} + (-1) \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 2 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} + (-1) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 2 \cdot (-1) = -2.$

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -4 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -6 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -4 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -6 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -1 \\ -4x_1-3x_2 = -6 \\ -7x_1-5x_2 =-11 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & -6 \\ -7 & -5 & -11 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ -7 & -5 & -11 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3+7R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & 9 & -18 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{1}{5} R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & -18 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 9 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -1 \\ x_2 = -2 \\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1+2(-2) = -1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=3. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3 \mathbf{a_1} + (-2) \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 3 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -4 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} + (-2) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -6 \\ -11 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 3 \cdot (-2) = -6.$

example.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.text:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a_2}$, $\mathbf{a_3}$, and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3 \}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b} = x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 + x_3 \mathbf{a}_3.$

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -8 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 18 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2}, \mathbf{a_3} \}$ if there exist $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ such that \begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}&= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -8 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 18 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-2x_3 = 3 \\ 4x_1+x_2-8x_3= 18 \\ 2x_1-3x_3 = 9 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -8 & 18 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 9 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:=R_2 - 4 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 9 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &:=R_3 - 2 R_1 \\[5pt] & \sim \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-2x_3 = 3 \\ x_2 = 6 \\ x_3 = 3. \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3=3.$ Substituting into the first equation gives

\[ x_1-2(3) = 3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=9. \]

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3 \}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$ and $\mathbf{a}_3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 9 \mathbf{a_1} + 6 \mathbf{a_2} + 3 \mathbf{a_3} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] 9 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + 6 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + 3 \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -8 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 18 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Finally, $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3 = 9 \cdot 6 \cdot 3 = 162.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Value of an Unknown Such That a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.text: Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -9 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -9 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+5x_2 = 3 \\ -2x_1-9x_2 = -4 \\ 2x_1+10x_2 = k \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & -9 & -4 \\ 2 & 10 & k \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 10 & k \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + (-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & k-6 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k-6.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if \[ 0 = k-6 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=6. \]

question.text: Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -5 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ -5 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1-4x_2 = 0 \\ 3x_1-5x_2 = 1 \\ 2x_1-4x_2 = k \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= \dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 3 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 2 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & k \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if \[ k=0. \]

question.text: Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where \[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ 3 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -9 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -2 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ 3 \\ -12 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -9 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} 6x_1-8x_2 = -3 \\ -2x_1+3x_2 = -9 \\ 10x_1-12x_2 = k \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & -8 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -9 \\ 10 & -12 & k \end{array}\right] & R_1 &\leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -2 & 3 & -9 \\ 6 & -8 & -3 \\ 10 & -12 & k \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -2 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & -30 \\ 10 & -12 & k \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + 5 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -2 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & -30 \\ 0 & 3 & k-45 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 3 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -2 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & -30 \\ 0 & 0 & k+45 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k+45.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if \[ 0 = k+45 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k=-45. \]

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k+9.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if \[ 0 = k+9 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=-9. \]

question.explanation:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\begin{align*} x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} &= \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 7 \\ 18 \\ 39 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -6 \\ k \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+7x_2 = -3 \\ 3x_1+18x_2 = -6 \\ 5x_1+39x_2 = k \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 3 & 18 & -6 \\ 5 & 39 & k \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + (-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 5 & 39 & k \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3+(-5)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & k+15 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= -\dfrac 1 3 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & k+15 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + (-4)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & k+19 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = k+19.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if \[ 0 = k+19 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k=-19. \]

question.text: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi : \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}$, $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbf{b}=\left\langle 1, 2, 3 \right\rangle$, $\mathbf{c} = \left\langle 3, 8, -7 \right\rangle$, and $\mathbf{u}= \langle 9, 22, -5 \rangle.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s \cdot t$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{u}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}.$
question.explanation:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} &= \mathbf{u} \\[5pt] s \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 8 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 22 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} s+3t= 9 \\ 2s+8t = 22\\ 3s-7t = -5 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 8 & 22 \\ 3 & -7 & -5 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2-2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 3 & -7 & -5 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3-3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -16 & -32 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + 8 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} s+3t= 9 \\ 2t = 4\\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get

\[ 2t = 4 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad t = 2. \]

Substituting into the first equation, we get

\begin{align*} s + 3t &= 9 \\[3pt] s + 3(2) &= 9 \\[3pt] s &= 3. \end{align*}

Since we found a solution $s=3, \, t=2,$ we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does indeed lie on the plane $\Pi.$ In fact, we have

\[ \mathbf{u}= 3\mathbf{b} + 2 \mathbf{c}. \]

Finally, $s\cdot t = 3 \cdot 2 = 6.$

question.text: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi: \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c},$ $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1, -2, -1 \rangle$, $\mathbf{c} = \langle -4, 5, -1 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{u}= \langle 1, 1, 4 \rangle.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s \cdot t$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{u}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}.$
question.explanation:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that \begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} &= \mathbf{u} \\[5pt] s \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 5 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} s-4t = 1 \\ -2s+5t = 1 \\ -s-t = 4 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 4 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + 2 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 4 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 5 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= -\dfrac{1}{3} R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -5 & 5 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 + 5 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} s-4t= 1 \\ t = -1\\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get

\[ t = -1. \]

Substituting into the first equation, we get

\begin{align*} s - 4t &= 1 \\[5pt] s - 4\left(-1\right) &= 1 \\[5pt] s + 4 &= 1 \\[5pt] s &= -3. \end{align*}

Since we found a solution $s=-3, \, t=-1,$ we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does indeed lie on the plane $\Pi.$ In fact, we have

\[ \mathbf{u}=-3\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{c}. \]

Finally, $s\cdot t = (-3) \cdot (-1) = 3.$

question.text: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi : \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c},$ $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1, 5, 8 \rangle$, $\mathbf{c} = \langle -1, -1, -3 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{u}= \langle -3, 5, -7 \rangle.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s \cdot t$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{u}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}.$
question.explanation:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} &= \mathbf{u} \\[5pt] s \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 5\\ 8 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 5 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} s-t = -3 \\ 5s-t = 5 \\ 8s-3t = -7 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,} \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & 5 \\ 8 & -3 & -7 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 -5 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4 & 20 \\ 8 & -3 & -7 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 -8 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4 & 20 \\ 0 & 5 & 17 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{1}{4}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 17 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 -5R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = -8,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} = \mathbf{u}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on the plane $\Pi.$

question.text: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi : \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}$, $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbf{b}=\left\langle -1, 4, 3 \right\rangle$, $\mathbf{c} = \left\langle 1, -6, -7 \right\rangle$, and $\mathbf{u}= \langle 1, -10, -15 \rangle.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s \cdot t$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{u}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}.$
question.explanation:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

\begin{align*} s \mathbf{b}+t \mathbf{c} &= \mathbf{u} \\[5pt] s \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + t \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -6 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -10 \\ -15 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of equations:

\[ \begin{cases} -s+t= 1 \\ 4s-6t = -10\\ 3s-7t = -15 \end{cases} \]

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

\begin{align*} &\phantom{\sim\,\,}\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -6 & -10 \\ 3 & -7 & -15 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 3 & -7 & -15 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3+3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -4 & -12 \end{array}\right] & R_3 &:= R_3 - 2 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

Now, we have the system

\[ \begin{cases} -s+t= 1 \\ -2t = -6\\ 0 = 0. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get

\[ -2t = -6 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad t = 3. \]

Substituting into the first equation, we get

\begin{align*} -s + t &= 1 \\[5pt] -s + 3 &= 1 \\[5pt] -s &= -2 \\[5pt] s &= 2. \end{align*}

Since we found a solution $s=2, \, t=3,$ we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does indeed lie on the plane $\Pi.$ In fact, we have

\[ \mathbf{u}=2\mathbf{b} + 3 \mathbf{c}. \]

Finally, $s\cdot t = 2 \cdot 3 = 6.$
